newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil- Firm on aggressive demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil- Firm on aggressive demand.

text.p: Continued demand from a local trading company kept the high sulphur fuel oil market firm on Wednesday and traders expected prices to stay firm in the near term.

The local buyer, who bought two 20,000-tonne cargoes of the 180-cst grade at $99.50 and $101 per tonne for April 9-13 and April 20-24 lifting respectively, bought another 20,000 tonnes at $101 per tonne for April 21-25 lifting.
Bids for the 180-cst grade went up to $101 per tonne from an initial $98.50, traders said.
"Judging from yesterday and today, I think he will continue buying and pushing prices higher," said one trader.
Several fuel oil tenders in the region also helped overall sentiment, traders said.
India has issued a tender to buy 30,000 tonnes of high sulphur fuel oil for delivery April 19-23. The tender will close April 23 and is valid for one day.
Another outstanding Indian tender for 30,000 tonnes closes on Wednesday and is valid until Thursday.
South Korea's KEDO also tendered to buy up to 64,000 tonnes of residual fuel.
But some traders remaind skeptical.

"There are still quite a few unsold cargoes but no fresh demand. I am not that optimistic about the rise," said one trader. "The only bullish factor is the maintenance turnaround season in the region."
Refineries in Japan, South Korea and China have entered their scheduled maintenance turnaround season in March.
